neighbours.label: In symptom/effect listings, the noun naming a bodily attribute right before an expected change-type noun (weight changes, appetite loss, sleep disturbances): the pole marks 'a change or problem word comes next'; quiet on plain lists of health items
fire: People with the condition often notice tiredness, weight gain and trouble concentrating.
Common side effects include nausea, appetite changes and dry mouth.
Shift workers frequently complain of headaches, sleep problems and low energy.
During pregnancy many women experience back pain, mood changes and swollen feet.
Early signs of the illness are fever, weight loss and night sweats.
The medication may lead to dizziness, vision changes and a dry cough.
Older patients sometimes report joint pain, memory loss and poor balance.
Stress can show up as stomach aches, appetite loss and trouble sleeping.
quiet: People with the condition often keep a diary, a pill box and a water bottle.
Common breakfast foods include porridge, toast and dried fruit.
Shift workers frequently bring sandwiches, coffee and warm clothes.
During pregnancy many women attend classes, read books and walk daily.
Early signs of spring are snowdrops, longer days and birdsong.
The pharmacy sells bandages, vitamins and a cough syrup.
Older patients sometimes bring a relative, a notebook and their glasses.
The nurse checked his pulse, his temperature and his breathing.

notes: Card: ' weight' (fluctuations), ' gender' (confirmation), ' eating' (disorder), ' health' (problems), ' iron' (deficiency); the - pole's output promotes ' change', ' changed', ' action'. Probes: 'weight changes' 0.43, 'appetite loss' 0.42, 'sleep disturbances' 0.35, 'blood pressure changes' 0.18, 'vitamin deficiency' 0.13; plain lists 0.00-0.03, 'anxiety disorder' 0.00. Top examples also include list commas and 'and', so this is probably part of the pole only.
